significance.justification: A verified-true result would establish that fabricated assistant turns produce a false self-authorship signal that "scal[es] with shot count," predicts jailbreak success beyond attention diffusion and imitation, and causally changes compliance; this combines a form-(iii) predictive/scaling relation with a form-(ii) mechanism rather than merely finding a jailbreak-related direction. The phenomenon is attribution-sensitive many-shot compliance, while the mechanism is a distinct self-authorship contributor; this would constrain explanations of why attack strength grows with demonstrations, an issue left mechanistically open by Anthropic's Many-shot Jailbreaking (2024), and would predict lower success when identical context is attributed to another source. Verified-false and verified-true are distinguishable: failure of the signal's incremental and bidirectional causal role would rule out self-authorship trust as a substantial account and leave imitation or attention diffusion carrying the explanation. In the topic-substitution check, generic mechanistic work on LLM safety would not earn this score; the score comes from the claim-specific attribution manipulation, shot-count law, and discrimination among competing mechanisms.

reach.justification: The named handle is "Self-Authorship Neutralization (SAN), a training-free defense steering injected context toward 'other-authored'," an inference-time intervention that acts ex ante on supplied history before the model answers, leaving a deployment action window rather than merely explaining a completed jailbreak. The claimed monotonic coupling among shot count, self-authorship projection, and attack success would survive per-model re-extraction as a predicted relation, although the exact direction and threshold would still require calibration. Scope is explicitly limited to chat-tuned models and many-shot or fabricated-history attacks, with effects potentially "strongest on open 7-9B chat models," but the conclusion is asserted across several model families and gives auditors or deployers a context filter rather than serving only mechanistic-interpretability researchers. The topic-substitution check does not preserve this score: general LLM-safety interpretability supplies neither SAN nor its before-response screening role, so the reach derives from this claim's reusable defensive handle.
